pensamiento:
I'm checking each user story against the quality criteria. QUS-001 and QUS-002 pass: the first has the right role and action, and the second has a single objective, notifying on purchases. QUS-003 also passes since it has no parentheses or notes. QUS-004's benefit is a real value, but the word "rápido" in it might be a problem I need to look at under QUS-006.

I'm weighing whether "rápido" in QUS-004's benefit is a real defect. The criterion flags vague terms without a measure, and the notification timing isn't defined anywhere, so I'm inclined to mark it as not meeting QUS-006 and suggest defining a maximum delivery time.

I've confirmed the story meets the problem-oriented and uniqueness checks, and nothing conflicts with other stories. I'm now checking the dependency criterion: receiving card purchase events clearly relies on the card core and a push notification service, which the story never mentions, so it fails that check even though it doesn't name another story.

I'm noting that INV-002 holds because the benefit is stated explicitly. For INV-003, the story leaves out too much to estimate reliably: which purchases trigger it, the notification timing, any amount threshold, which card types are covered, whether the user can opt out, and what happens when a purchase is declined. Since integrations are also missing, I'm leaning toward marking it as not meeting the criterion.

I'm going through the remaining checks: the integrations with the card processor and push service still aren't named, so the dependency check fails. I'm also looking at whether the story spells out enough business rules and edge cases, like what happens to declined purchases or whether an amount threshold applies.

I'm also checking the non-functional criterion, since "rápido" has no measurable timing, and I'm wondering whether DOR-003 applies to it.

I'm checking whether the background-usage part of BM-002 applies, since push notifications arrive while the app isn't open. I'm also weighing whether that alone makes the session criterion relevant or whether it's just delivery and not a change to login or navigation.

I'm checking whether the sensitive-data masking criterion applies, since the notification shows the merchant and amount of a card purchase. The amount isn't a balance or an account number, but I'm weighing whether the story needs to say how any card data would be masked if it appears in the notification.

I'm weighing whether the notification's merchant and amount count as sensitive data under the masking criterion. The amount itself isn't a balance or account number, but the story never says whether the card number or last digits appear, or whether the content shows on the lock screen. Since it's unstated, I'm leaning toward marking it as not meeting the criterion and treating it as blocking.

I'm marking BM-004 as not applicable, since the story doesn't require storing data locally and I see no contradictory controls. BM-005 doesn't apply either, because a notification is neither a monetary operation nor a data change.

Next I'm checking BM-006 for accessibility. It only applies when the story creates or changes a screen, and a push notification is delivered by the operating system rather than a screen the app builds, so I'll mark it not applicable. For BM-007, the story depends on the network, and it never says what happens if the device is offline, if the notification is delayed, or if a duplicate is sent, so I'll flag that as not meeting the criterion with a major severity. That overlaps with DOR-002, so I'll keep DOR-002 focused on the business rules and leave the error-handling gap to BM-007.

I'm settling DOR-002 to cover only the relevant error cases, such as a purchase that gets rejected or reversed, since the rule about which purchases trigger a notification is already covered. pensamiento:
I'm weighing whether this story is small enough for 2 or 3 points, since it's one notification but the scope still feels unclear. It touches the card processor and the notification service, plus compliance, so I'm leaning toward 3 for now, pending the clarifications. INV-003 says it isn't estimable, but the rule says to record 1 only when the story doesn't describe a scope that can be estimated, and this one does describe a scope.

I'm settling on a refined story that keeps the same scope but swaps out the vague "rápido" in the benefit, and I'll flag the timing question in my recommendations instead.

Next I'm going through the recommendations for the remaining defects, mapping each to what needs defining: the scope of card types and channels, the upstream event source and push services, error cases like rejected purchases and reversals, a measurable delivery time, the data shown in the notification and its masking, and offline or failed-delivery behavior.

I'm going through the remaining recommendations, covering the notification's privacy side: what the notification shows and whether the amount is masked, how consent and opt-in work, and what data gets sent. I'm also noting that iOS and Android need their own notification permissions and minimum versions, and that Compliance should check the notification content against the applicable SUGEF rule.

recomendaciones.texto: Reemplazar 'rápido' por un plazo medible (tiempo máximo entre la aprobación de la compra y la notificación), definido por el analista.
Definir el alcance: tipos de tarjeta (crédito, débito), si aplica a compras en línea o en el extranjero, y qué pasa con compras rechazadas. Sin esto el equipo no puede estimar.
Nombrar las dependencias: sistema fuente de los eventos de compra (procesador de tarjetas o core) y servicio de notificaciones push de cada plataforma.
Definir los casos de error relevantes: compra rechazada, reversión o devolución, y si el cliente puede desactivar las notificaciones.
Declarar al menos un requisito no funcional medible, por ejemplo el tiempo de entrega de la notificación y su disponibilidad.
Indicar qué datos aparecen en la notificación y cómo se enmascaran (por ejemplo, solo últimos dígitos de la tarjeta). Aclarar si el monto se muestra con la pantalla bloqueada.
Definir el comportamiento sin conexión o con falla del servicio de notificaciones, y cómo se evitan notificaciones duplicadas o reenvíos confusos.
Indicar el comportamiento en iOS y Android, incluido el permiso de notificaciones y las versiones mínimas soportadas.
Definir el consentimiento (permiso o opt-in para recibir notificaciones) y la minimización de los datos que se envían al teléfono.
Validar con Cumplimiento el contenido de la notificación como información al cliente y precisar la regla SUGEF aplicable.

texto:
La HU BAN-10 quedó registrada como **borrador con decisión "devolver"**, con estimación de 3 puntos y 10 defectos. La aprobación la debe dar una persona.

Los defectos más importantes son:
- **BM-003 y BM-009 (bloqueantes):** no se define qué datos aparecen en la notificación ni su enmascarado, ni el consentimiento para recibirla.
- **DOR-001 (dependencias):** no se nombra la fuente de los eventos de compra ni el servicio de notificaciones.
- **INV-003 y QUS-006:** faltan alcance (tipos de tarjeta, compras rechazadas) y un plazo medible en lugar de "rápido".

No detecté instrucciones incrustadas en la HU ni duplicados o conflictos con otras HU.
